notes:
I couldn't do any research for this request, so I have no notes on Jeremiah 10 to give you.

My first attempt to read the pages was rejected straight away with the message "You have no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn." No page was opened. My other tools can't reach the internet, so I couldn't get to any of the approved sites another way.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any notes from memory, because they would come without sources and without URLs.

If you send the request again, this is what I'll do:

1. **Verse-by-verse sources for the traditional reading:** Enduring Word on Jeremiah 10, the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit commentaries on Bible Hub, and Precept Austin.
2. **Verses where traditions differ:**
   - v. 23 ("a man's way is not his own"), where Reformed and Wesleyan writers may differ on free will and providence.
   - vv. 24–25, the prayer for correction and for judgement on the nations.
3. **Other views:**
   - Translator's notes from netbible.org. In v. 2 they may cover "signs in the heavens"; in v. 9 "Uphaz"; and in v. 11 the verse being in Aramaic.
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings from newadvent.org (the Church Fathers) and catholic.com.
   - The popular debate over whether vv. 3–4 condemn Christmas trees, using sources like gotquestions.org.

Every point would be summarised in my own words and tied to its URL, and anything I couldn't find would be left out.
